source_text: Ac per hoc secundum argumentationem quoque tuam olim non est, secundum testimonium veritatis numquam fuit.
pass_a_gloss: And through this according to your argumentation also it has long not been, according to the testimony of truth it never was.
pass_b_english: Consequently, even according to your argument, it ceased to exist long ago; according to the testimony of truth, it never existed.

choices.why: Proof-text, especially Rom 5:12 in this book; keep 'testimony' not 'verse'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
